questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The ranking of the university and the city itself.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was not really any information for exchange students in the beginning of the semester, so you mostly had to figure things out yourself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance upon arrival

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: As long as you're looking early on, the opportunities are alright, but still quite expensive. I found housing through Airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is not the best in Toronto, especially when living far east or far west in the city. So consider looking into that before finding off campus housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process comes in multiple rounds, where you fill out your course requests in a Google Analytics formula each time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The description of the registration process in the email is very thorough and easy to follow.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the requested classes during the first round, so it was quite easy to choose courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to look out for the course request deadline as it is only a window of about one week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is probably quite high by North American standards and a lot of people are very ambitious, but the style of teaching is very different from what we are used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. The courses are much more about calculations and doing things without aids, and much less about intuition and actual understanding of the course material, which we are used to at UCPH. However, this is probably just the way things are in North America.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Monetary Economics 
Advanced Microeconomics - Game Theory 
Introductory Philosophy of Science 
Markets, Competition and Strategy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Monetary Economics is a very good course to take, and the professor is really good at teaching and explaining.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Phone service is expensive in Canada (around 300 kr per month for a basic subscription).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks are pretty much the same price as in Denmark, so a bit more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have different athletic clubs and social clubs, but there are so many that it is difficult to find out what the best things are.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The nature outside the city is really cool - I can definitely recommend seeing Niagara Falls and going to Algonquin National Park, which is about three hours by car from Toronto.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy given the English language and the similarities to Danish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: U of T is not a very social university, so I think the best way is to participate in some of the social clubs and activities around campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not anything in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Not anything in particular

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Look for housing as early as possible 
Read travel reports about courses before deciding as they differ a lot in quality 
Look for public transportation options before deciding on housing

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything I haven't mentioned

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is a great experience to live in another country and to live in a city that is so much bigger than Copenhagen

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Since people speak English and most things are pretty similar to things in Denmark, I wouldn't say that there are a lot of challenges

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
